name: NY Tech Meetup: Neuro+HealthTech Edition
why: Monthly NYC tech meetup featuring demos and talks focused on neuroscience and health technology startups.

name: Quantum Computing Meetup
why: Drew Parker of Dainamiq leads a quantum computing session at Microsoft's NYC office.

name: Deconstructing The Twilight Zone: Sci-Fi Predicted Our AI Future
why: Author and designer Arlen Schumer explores how Rod Serling's 1960s sci-fi anthology anticipated modern AI dilemmas.

name: Contemporaneous Ensemble Open Mic
why: New music ensemble performs works by a dozen composers, all submitted through an open call.

name: Franklin Park Reading Series
why: Readings from authors Hannah Lilith Assadi, Nora Lange, Andrew Martin, Giada Scodellaro, and Deena Elgenaidi. Books from Unnameable Books.

name: The Lab: Improv Comedy Inspired by Real Science
why: Performers interview a real scientist, then use their expertise as inspiration for completely made-up improv comedy.

name: Marcel Duchamp at MoMA
why: The first U.S. retrospective of Duchamp's work since 1973, featuring 300 works spanning his full career from 1900 to 1968.

name: Claude Code Meetup For Developers
why: Builders share demos of projects built with Claude Code, followed by a live Q&A with the Anthropic team.

name: Grieving & Weaving
why: Knitting, crocheting, and crafting in a cemetery chapel, sharing stories and grief resources. All skill levels welcome.

name: A Better World Is Possible: Youth Confront Climate Crisis
why: Danica Novgorodoff and Meera Subramanian present their book on global youth climate action, in conversation with activists Jamie Margolin and Shiv Soin.

name: Brooklyn Museum Gallery Tours
why: Expert-led tours highlighting favorites from the museum's collection, running Wednesday through Friday at 1pm.

name: AI Startup Founder Pitch Night
why: Early-stage AI startup founders pitch their ideas to an audience of investors and fellow builders.

name: The Pickled City: Tasting & Discussion
why: Tasting and discussion tracing the brined cucumber from ancient Mesopotamia to the Lower East Side, with access to the Street Food City exhibition.

name: The Alchemy of Movement Building
why: A panel on what meaningful action looks like, moderated by Saul Austerlitz, author of How to Assemble an Activist.

name: Brooklyn Museum Pop-Up Talks
why: Brief, informal talks by museum educators in the galleries, running Wednesday through Friday.

name: Urbani Truffle Lab After-Hours Experience
why: An exclusive after-hours tasting experience inside the Urbani truffle lab, getting up close and personal with truffles.

name: Out In Tech: Queer Tech Stories Across Generations
why: Queer technologists share stories spanning generations of LGBTQ+ experience in the tech industry, hosted at Spotify's NYC headquarters.

name: Possibilities in Theory
why: Artist Gregg Bordowitz reflects on how French Theory by Barthes, Derrida, and Foucault opened new possibilities for New York artists of the 80s and 90s.

name: The Modernity of Antiquity: Karl Lagerfeld & Greek Art
why: Williams College professor Christophe Kone examines Karl Lagerfeld's fascination with Greek Antiquity through Chanel's 2017/18 Cruise collection.

name: Grand Opening: The Green-House at Green-Wood
why: Opening weekend for Green-Wood's newest space, with hands-on workshops, guided explorations, and programs for all ages.

name: Grand Opening: The Green-House at Green-Wood
why: Opening weekend for Green-Wood's newest space, with hands-on workshops, guided explorations, and programs for all ages.

name: Generative Media Hackathon
why: A hackathon inviting developers and creators to build generative media projects, powered by ElevenLabs.

name: Renegade Craft: Spring Fair
why: The indie craft fair returns with handmade goods, local artisans, and a curated marketplace of one-of-a-kind finds.

name: The Quiet Car: Turn the Q Train Quiet
venue: Q Train (96th St to Canal St)
why: Celebrate the launch of Quietest Places in New York by creating a quiet car ride on the Q train. Bring an analog activity; RSVP gets a free copy of the book.

name: Woolworth Building Behind-the-Scenes Tour
why: An exclusive behind-the-scenes tour inside the Woolworth Building, one of NYC's most stunning architectural landmarks.

name: Vintage Festival: Day + Night Market
why: A two-day vintage market featuring thrifted finds and collectibles from curated vendors in East Williamsburg.

name: Folk Nation: Crafting Patriotism
why: New exhibition exploring how folk artists have expressed patriotism across centuries, alongside Self-Made: A Century of Inventing Artists.

name: Kitchen Arts & Letters Book Clean-Out Sale
why: Hundreds of damaged, used, and well-loved food and drink books priced $1-20 at the legendary culinary bookshop's annual clean-out.

name: NYC Buskerball
why: An all-day outdoor festival celebrating busking musicians, poets, dancers, and street performers in Tompkins Square Park.

name: Crafting Community: A Textile Arts Fair
why: A textile arts fair bringing together fiber artists, weavers, and makers for a day of crafting and community.

name: Drop-In Workshops: Life at Sea
why: Drop-in art-making workshops inspired by the museum's maritime collection. All ages and skill levels welcome.

name: Keith Haring: On the Street
why: Two of Keith Haring's painted cars on view in a former 19th-century carriage house, alongside original works, photographs, and the book Keith Haring in 3D.

name: Discover Green-Wood Trolley Tour
why: An expert-led trolley tour through 478 acres of Green-Wood's historic landscape and its most intriguing permanent residents.

name: Highbridge Water Tower Tour
why: A rare chance to peek inside the historic Highbridge Water Tower and take in the panoramic view from 200 feet up.

name: Bargemusic: Mozart String Quartets
venue: Bargemusic at Brooklyn Bridge Park Pier 5
why: Chamber music on the water with floor-to-ceiling views of the East River and Lower Manhattan skyline. Opening weekend features Mozart selections.

name: Modern Whitney: Comedians Interpret Art
why: Comedians give their own takes on a piece of art before a professional expert swoops in to set the record straight.

name: Streb: Into Thin Air
why: Elizabeth Streb's extreme action ensemble executes choreographed feats of split-second ducking, dodging, trampolines, retractable ramps, and suspended parallel bars.

name: The Travel Companion (Premiere + Q&A)
why: BAM presents the premiere of Alex Mallis and Travis Wood's feature debut, followed by a Q&A with the filmmakers.

name: Bad Movie Night: Crocodile Fury
why: Revel in the so-bad-it's-good chaos of Godfrey Ho's Crocodile Fury (1988) with fellow bad movie fans at a Gowanus brewery.

name: Birding in Peace at Green-Wood
why: An early morning walking tour with special pre-opening access. April brings pine warblers, woodpeckers, and thousands of migrating songbirds.

name: Vibe FORWARD Hackathon
why: Developers, designers, and NYU researchers gather to create and demo prototypes using AI tools from Lovable and Tavily.

name: Jackie Robinson's Brooklyn Legacy Tour
why: A walking tour from Prospect Park to the site of Ebbets Field, exploring Brooklyn baseball history and Jackie Robinson breaking the color barrier.

name: Pioneer Works Second Sundays
why: Free monthly open house with programming across art, music, science, and community spread across three floors and the garden.

name: East Village Dark Side Tour
why: Uncover the East Village's dark side through music, art, and haunting history on a walking tour of the neighborhood.

name: Greenpointers Spring Market
why: Spring market with rooftop views, $5 drinks, 65 local vendors, and free activities for all ages at Greenpoint Loft.

name: Brooklyn Taco Takedown
why: Chefs compete to make the best taco in Brooklyn, with unlimited tasting for attendees at this Gowanus shuffleboard club.

name: Brooklyn Symphony Orchestra Pop-Up
why: A free pop-up performance by the Brooklyn Symphony Orchestra inside the museum galleries.

name: Some Fun Lines: Satire & Humor Showcase
why: Writers from The New Yorker, McSweeney's, and the John Oliver show perform slideshows, games, and readings with guest readers.

name: Public Victories Storytelling
why: Four performers and one audience member share true stories of personal triumphs, from running the dishwasher to running a marathon.

name: Woody Fu: One Man John Wick
why: Actor and comedian Woody Fu dons a $15 wig to channel Keanu Reeves in this scripted solo show that turns the stage into a DIY action movie set.
